questions.title: 61. Why do we need useCallback?
questions.summary:
◦ useCallback caches a F() ref between re-r()s.
◦ Useful for stable cb^ props and H^ deps.
questions.answer:
◦ useCallback = R^ H^ that caches a F() ref between renders.
◦ Returns the same F() when deps remain unchanged.
◦ Prevents unnecessary ref changes for cb^ props.
◦ Useful when passing cb^s to memoized C^s.
◦ Useful when a stable F() is required by another H^.
◦ Does not prevent the parent C^ from re-r().
◦ Use only when stable identity provides a measurable benefit.
questions.underTheHood:
◦ R^ stores cb^ + deps in the owning C^ Fiber-associated H^ data.
◦ During re-r(), R^ compares deps using Object.is().
◦ Unchanged deps → Return cached F() ref.
◦ Changed deps → Store + return new F().
◦ React.memo can skip child re-r() when its props remain equal.
◦ Stable cb^ ref helps avoid invalidating memoization.
pitfalls: ◦ useCallback does not prevent F() creation during r().
◦ useCallback does not automatically improve perf_nc.
◦ Missing deps can produce stale closures.
◦ New object/array props may still cause child re-r().
◦ React.memo is not required for every useCallback use case.
questions.recall:
◦ useCallback(F(), deps) → Stable F() ref.
◦ deps = → Reuse.
◦ deps ≠ → Replace.
◦ React.memo + Stable cb^ → Possible skipped child re-r().
